text: PointShape.Diamond added in 65bc425. A square rotated 45 degrees whose area equals the Circle at the same size: half-diagonal r*sqrt(pi/2), so 2d^2 = pi r^2, exposed as PointShape.diamondHalfDiagonal. Device.shapeMarks lowers it to a closed four-vertex polyline on the axes; SVG (Points and PointBatch), Canvas, Java2D, JavaFX and PDF draw it from their point-batch shape matches. RendererConformance.shapeCase covers it, so every backend harness proves it. PointShapeLaws pins centring for every shape, diamond/circle area parity via the shoelace area of the lowered vertices, and the diamond's axis-aligned hit-test bounds; docs/style-aesthetics.md carries the shape table and the formula. Area parity was confirmed by the storyatlas4s session as what the voyage plate wants: the plate encodes posterior mass as mark area, so a decode-bound anchor must read as the same quantity of ink as a posterior-argmax anchor of equal mass. Consequence recorded in CHANGELOG.md and MIGRATION.md: Diamond is the one shape that extends past the [-r, r] box, so a backend assuming a point mark fits that box must widen the assumption. Not established: no pinned raster golden or paired ggplot2 visual-QA case shows a diamond; no backend hit-tests points, the law only pins the bounds a hit-test would use; the equal-area rule is not applied retroactively to Square or Triangle.
